title: Statistics
fromLiveGames: {count, plural, one {from # live game} other {from # live games}}
filterSummary: {filtered} of {total} {total, plural, one {game} other {games}} in the filter.
noGamesInFilter: No games in the current filter.

overview.fromLiveRoles: {count, plural, one {from # live role} other {from # live roles}}
overview.whoWinsInfo: Every game belongs to exactly one winner group — so the shares add up to 100%.
overview.deathsInfo: Live games only — quick entry doesn't record a cause of death. The color shows who is responsible: red for the wolves, blue for the village — as in the winner distribution.
overview.deathsEmpty: No causes of death recorded yet (only live games provide them).
overview.monthlyInfo: Bar height = number of games, colors = who won. Counts instead of rates on purpose: with only a few games a month, a rate would jump between 0% and 100%.
overview.revealInfo: House rule of live games: is a person's card shown after they die? Only live games have this setting. Games not recorded date from before the setting existed and are not silently counted as hidden.

players.highlightsInfo: Superlatives over the selected period. Rows based on a rate only appear from {minSample} observations — below that the rate would be chance.
players.highlightsEmpty: Not enough data for superlatives yet.
players.allInfo: A character portrait instead of a ranking: how often they play, how successful they are per side, how often they survive, which role they like best. The placement is on the leaderboard page.
players.survivedInfo: Share of live games this person made it to the end of. A dash means there is no live data.
players.distinctRoles: {count, plural, one {# different role} other {# different roles}}
players.note: V/W/S = win rate as village / werewolves / solo; the number after the dot is the sample size. Without it you couldn't see that a "100%" can come from a single game.

roles.title: Roles
roles.info: Δ compares the role's win rate with the win rate of its own faction across all games. A village role at 50% is unremarkable if the village wins 50% anyway — only the deviation tells you whether the role helps its side.
roles.noteWithDelta: Δ is measured against the faction win rate. Avg. death = average round of death (0 = first night).
roles.note: Avg. death = average round of death (0 = first night).
roles.showHidden: Show {hidden, plural, one {# role} other {# roles}} with fewer than {min} games
roles.heatmapInfo: Win rate per player and role. Red = low, green = high, number = number of games. Limited to the most-played roles, otherwise the matrix would be unreadably wide.
roles.heatmapCell: {player} as {role}: {rate} across {games, plural, one {# game} other {# games}}
roles.heatmapNote: {count, plural, one {The most-played role} other {The # most-played roles}}. A single game in a cell is not a signal — so the number always shows the sample size.

compare.headToHeadInfo: Two players side by side, plus how often they were on the same or on opposing teams and who won then.
compare.alliesInfo: Sorted by the absolute number of shared wins or losses — not by rate, otherwise a fellow player from two games at 100% would rank above one from twenty at 75%.
compare.rateOfGames: {rate} across {games, plural, one {# game} other {# games}}
